title: Stripe
content:
## Overview

Stripe is a payment processing platform that enables your Emergent app to accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle complex billing scenarios. This guide walks you through integrating Stripe into your project using Emergent's natural language interface.

<Note>
Stripe integration requires a Stripe account. You can create one at [stripe.com](https://stripe.com) and use test mode during development at no cost.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Stripe, ensure you have:

- A Stripe account (test mode credentials work for development)
- Your Stripe **Publishable Key** (starts with `pk_`)
- Your Stripe **Secret Key** (starts with `sk_`)
- A clear understanding of what payment flows your app needs (one-time payments, subscriptions, etc.)

## Integration Steps

<Steps>
<Step title="Tell Emergent about your payment needs">
Describe your payment requirements in natural language. Be specific about what you want to accomplish:

**Example prompts:**
- "Add Stripe payment processing. Users should be able to purchase credits for $10, $25, or $50."
- "Integrate Stripe subscriptions with three tiers: Basic ($9/month), Pro ($29/month), and Enterprise ($99/month)."
- "Add a checkout flow where users can buy individual products from a catalog."

Emergent's agents will generate the appropriate Stripe integration code, including client-side checkout components and server-side payment endpoints.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide your Stripe API keys">
Once the integration code is generated, you'll need to add your Stripe credentials as environment variables.

In your Emergent project, tell the agent:

```
Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to sk_test_xxxxx
Set STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to pk_test_xxxxx
```

<Warning>
Never commit secret keys to your codebase. Use Emergent's environment variable system to keep credentials secure. In production, replace test keys (`sk_test_`, `pk_test_`) with live keys (`sk_live_`, `pk_live_`).
</Warning>

The agent will configure these as secure environment variables accessible to your backend code.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the payment flow">
Ask Emergent to test the integration:

```
Test the Stripe checkout flow
```

The agents will verify that:
- Checkout sessions are created correctly
- Payment confirmation webhooks are received
- Success and cancellation redirects work as expected

Use [Stripe's test card numbers](https://stripe.com/docs/testing) to simulate successful and failed payments during testing.
</Step>

<Step title="Handle webhooks">
For production-grade integrations, configure webhook handling. Tell Emergent:

```
Set up Stripe webhooks to handle payment confirmation and subscription events
```

The agent will:
- Create webhook endpoints in your backend
- Parse and verify Stripe webhook signatures
- Update your database based on payment events

You'll receive a webhook URL to add in your Stripe Dashboard under **Developers → Webhooks**.
</Step>

<Step title="Deploy to production">
When you're ready to go live:

1. Replace test API keys with live keys in your environment variables
2. Update webhook endpoints in your Stripe Dashboard to point to your production domain
3. Ensure your [custom domain](/custom-domain) is configured if using one

Ask Emergent: `Deploy the app with production Stripe keys`
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common Payment Patterns

<Tabs>
<Tab title="One-time payments">
For simple product purchases or one-off charges:

```
Add a "Buy Now" button that charges $49.99 for premium access
```

Emergent will create a Stripe Checkout session that handles the entire payment flow, including success/cancel redirects.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Subscriptions">
For recurring billing:

```
Create a subscription system with monthly and annual billing options
```

The agents will set up Stripe subscription products, handle plan changes, and manage billing cycles.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Usage-based billing">
For metered or consumption-based pricing:

```
Set up usage-based billing where users are charged $0.10 per API call
```

This creates a metered billing system that reports usage to Stripe and bills accordingly.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Payment links">
For simple no-code payment collection:

```
Generate a Stripe payment link for a $199 consulting package
```

Returns a shareable URL that you can use in emails, marketing pages, or chat messages.
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Refining Your Integration

After the initial setup, you can refine the integration with natural language:

- "Add a customer portal where users can manage their subscription and update payment methods"
- "Show a payment history page with all past invoices"
- "Add a discount code field to the checkout"
- "Send a confirmation email after successful payment"
- "Store customer payment info for future purchases"

## Security Best Practices

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Use webhooks" icon="webhook">
Don't rely solely on client-side success callbacks. Webhooks provide authoritative, server-verified payment confirmation.
</Card>

<Card title="Validate amounts server-side" icon="shield-check">
Never trust payment amounts from the client. Always define prices and calculations in backend code.
</Card>

<Card title="Test failure scenarios" icon="alert-triangle">
Use Stripe's test cards to simulate declined payments, insufficient funds, and fraud scenarios.
</Card>

<Card title="Handle idempotency" icon="repeat">
Stripe operations should be idempotent to prevent duplicate charges if requests are retried.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Payments succeed but webhooks aren't received">
Verify your webhook URL is publicly accessible and correctly configured in the Stripe Dashboard. During local development, use Stripe CLI to forward webhooks to localhost, or ask Emergent: `Set up local webhook testing for Stripe`
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Invalid API key errors">
Double-check that you're using the correct key type (publishable keys for frontend, secret keys for backend) and that they match your Stripe account mode (test vs. live).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Checkout session expires too quickly">
Stripe Checkout sessions expire after 24 hours by default. If users abandon checkout frequently, consider storing session state and allowing them to resume, or create a new session on return.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Currency or region issues">
Stripe supports 135+ currencies but availability varies by country. Tell Emergent which currencies and regions you need to support: `Configure Stripe to accept EUR and GBP in addition to USD`
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next Steps

<Card title="Database Integration" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Store payment records and subscription status in your MongoDB database
</Card>

<Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Configure a custom domain for professional payment page branding
</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Info>
Stripe's pricing is pay-as-you-go with no monthly fees. You're charged a percentage of each successful transaction. Check [Stripe's pricing page](https://stripe.com/pricing) for current rates in your region.
</Info>
